final_answer: Hypothesis: Increased education spending does not positively impact per capita GDP in Sub-Saharan Africa and Lower middle income countries. The context of this hypothesis is based on the dataset that contains information on government expenditure on education and per capita GDP for these regions. The variables chosen are 'Adjusted savings: education expenditure (percentage of GNI)' and 'GNI per capita (constant 2015 US dollar)'. The analysis shows a strong negative correlation between these variables in Sub-Saharan Africa (-0.966) and a moderate negative correlation in Lower middle income countries (-0.481), indicating that increased education spending does not lead to an increase in per capita GDP in these regions.
